newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission changes proposal on procurement.
newsitem.headline: Commission changes proposal on procurement.

text.p: The European Commission agreed on Wednesday to amend its proposal to adapt the EU's public procurement directives to take account of the Government Procurement Agreement operated within the World Trade Organisation.
The proposal concerns the directives on the so-called "excluded sectors" of water, energy, transport and telecommunications.

The modification comes after a battle between the Commission and the European Parliament, which feared the modifications previously proposed would give third country suppliers an advantage in fighting for contracts on offer in the EU.
The Commission stressed in a statement the outcome of the proposed modifications would not be to give third country suppliers better access than EU suppliers, rather the opposite.
"The aim is to ensure that third country suppliers do not enjoy better access to contracts than Community suppliers," the statement said.
It said the aim was also to introduce more flexibility into the technical dialogue between suppliers and procurement entities.
"This proposal does not in any way constitute a unilateral opening of EU markets to companies from third countries."

It said the proposal had been amended to make clear that the directive would not open up the EU market any further to suppliers from third countries by clarifying the fields of application of the directive and the GPA.

It has also reworded the text on technical dialogue to make it more flexible and limit to the sectors covered by the GPA the obligation to inform eliminated candidates or tenderers of the reasons for their rejection and the characteristics and advantages of the tenderer selected.
